reasons.ruby-state: These cases check Ruby object mechanics with no Tanvo counterpart: the aggregation state the aggregators write on a store (aggregation_property, numeric_property) is part of metering.Request, and a metering.BucketTotal slice is a value the store returns, with no shared accumulator to freeze or copy.
reasons.any-window: lago's bucket store answers only the prefetched charges window and mints a plain store for any other one (for_window). Tanvo's metering.UsageBucketStore answers any window exactly, reading the partial buckets at its edges from the events (TestUsageBucketStoreCombines), so there is no sibling window to hand over.
reasons.served-empty: UsageBucketSet#empty? backs the fallback of lago's provider when the set is empty, because a lagging RisingWave pipeline cannot be told apart from no usage (provider.rb:107-110). Tanvo's buckets are written in the same write as the events (parity §3, RisingWave row), so a ready definition with no rows is no usage and is served; a definition that is not ready yet answers ok=false and the events serve it (TestUsageBucketStoreAnswers).
reasons.prefetch: lago prefetches the buckets of every servable charge of the plan in one read keyed by charge and charge filter IDs (FetchBucketsService, charge_filter_ids_for). Tanvo's buckets are keyed by the metric's property dimensions, not by charge, and each charge bucket reads its own totals (metering.BucketRead), so there are no charge or filter IDs to list and no plan-wide read.
reasons.pipeline: The default concerns the rows RisingWave writes without a precise amount. Tanvo's stores write every bucket with its amount, units and events count (buckettest), so no row lacks one.
reasons.sink: Delete markers are how the RisingWave sink retracts a row from the ReplacingMergeTree. Tanvo's stores maintain the buckets in the event write and correct a replaced event in place (buckettest "replace corrects the bucket"), so no retracted row exists to skip.
reasons.sink-table: These cases check the ActiveRecord model of the RisingWave sink table (its factory, table name, primary key, FINAL reads, read-only guard and nullable plan and wallet columns). Tanvo's bucket tables are owned and written by libs/eventstore, whose schema and behaviour are checked by the buckettest conformance suite on PostgreSQL and ClickHouse; buckets are keyed by dimensions, so there is no plan or target wallet column.
reasons.same-store: lago reads its buckets from ClickHouse next to an events store it can fall back to. Tanvo's buckets live in the event store itself, so an outage of the bucket read is an outage of the events read too: the error is returned with %w rather than reported and swallowed, and every read of the store, the buckets' included, goes through the store's own retry and connection handling.
reasons.query-shape: These cases check the SQL lago emits against usage_buckets_15m (its sort order prefix, FINAL, delete marker and charge ID list). Tanvo's queries are per definition and dimension and are checked by their results in buckettest, not their text.
reasons.no-gate: Tanvo ships realtime usage without lago's organization flag, kill switch, premium license or forced gate (parity §1.50 and the feature flag row): a store that keeps usage buckets serves them, and a store without them answers ErrBucketsUnavailable, which the billing side treats as "read the events" (libs/billing DefineUsageBuckets).
reasons.postgres-buckets: lago keeps buckets only for organizations on the ClickHouse events store. Tanvo's PostgreSQL store keeps the same buckets in the same write as its events (buckettest runs on both stores), so a PostgreSQL organization is served from them too and the buckets cannot disagree with its events.
reasons.validation: This case checks the charge properties validation refusing a latest metric on a graduated_percentage charge; Tanvo ports that validation in the charge validation (pricing.ValidateOptions.LatestAggregation, set by libs/billing/plans/charges.go), not in the bucket classification, which never sees such a charge.
reasons.store-factory: lago's provider builds an events store per aggregation (store_for), forwarding the window, the filters and the per-charge state, and picks its class and deduplication per organization (store_class, deduplicate, the store override). Tanvo has one event store per deployment (architecture §7.4), which always deduplicates at ingestion, and every aggregation hands it its whole metering.Request value, so there is no store to configure, share or pick.
reasons.segment: A billing segment is priced through its product rate card (libs/billing/fees ProductSegment), which never sets metering.Request.UsageBuckets; only the charges of a plan reach the bucket gate (fees.servedFromBuckets), as in lago.
reasons.prefilter: lago lists the charge filters the buckets hold usage for, so that a charge served whole skips the events store query that resolves the billing period's filters (serves_whole_charge_from_buckets?, precomputed_filter_ids). Tanvo has no such pre-filter query: every charge bucket is aggregated through the bucket gate, and the filters without units are dropped afterwards (usage.Options.SkipZeroUnitsFilters).
reasons.cutover: The comparison service, the duplicate counter and the rake task compare the RisingWave buckets with the events store to decide when an organization can be cut over to the buckets. Tanvo's buckets are written in the same write as the events and reads are exact at the window edges (parity §3, RisingWave row), so there is no second source to compare and no cutover; the conformance suites (buckettest, storetest bucket specs) and TestCurrentUsageFromBuckets check that the buckets and the events agree.
